chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When one of you is invited to food, let him not send his son ahead (to eat before the host is ready or before the meal is served), for if he does so, he eats what is forbidden and enters as a usurper.

key_terms.حَرَامًا: forbidden (in this context, food eaten without right or permission)
key_terms.غَاصِبًا: usurper (one who takes what is not rightfully theirs)
key_terms.يَسْتَتْبِعَنَّ: to send ahead (specifically a child or servant to prepare or eat)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sending children ahead to eat when invited to a meal?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that sending a child ahead to eat before the host's explicit invitation constitutes 'ghasb' (usurping the right of the host) and renders the consumption 'haram' due to lack of proper consent. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that hospitality rights are tied to the host's will, and premature consumption violates the social contract of the meal. It serves as a practical lesson in adab (etiquette), ensuring guests do not overstep boundaries or assume entitlement before being formally welcomed.
